sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

items.prompt: A rental charges a $10 base fee plus $5 per hour, totaling $35. Which equation models this, and how many hours were rented?

steps: Identify what the problem is asking and which quantities, assumptions, or constraints matter.
Build and solve a model, then check the result against the context.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A diver starts at the surface (0 m) and descends 6 m, then descends another 8 m, then ascends 3 m. The dive plan assumes a depth limit of 29 m below the surface. What is the diver's final position, as a signed number of meters?
A model predicts a $680 rate will increase by 5%. What does the model predict as the new rate?
A storage container is designed as a rectangular prism 8 ft long, 10 ft wide, and 8 ft high. What is its volume in cubic feet?
A data set has the values 30, 45, 60, 75, 90. The mean is 60. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD), a measure of the data's uncertainty or spread?
A student claims a box that is 8 by 7 by 6 units has a volume of 56 cubic units. Evaluate the claim.
choices: Cannot be determined from the given information.
No; the volume is 336 cubic units, not 56.
No; the volume is 57 cubic units, not 56.
Yes; the volume is 56 cubic units.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: A rental company charges a $9 base fee plus $5 per hour. A customer's total bill was $34. Which equation models this situation, and how many hours were rented?
